title: Interleg ankle-brachial index asymmetry did not improve transferred prediction of measured gait speed beyond minimum ABI
abstract: In public NHANES1999–2000 adults aged50+(n1453), a frozen model tested in separately recruited NHANES2001–2002(n1598) showed no predictive gain from absolute interleg ABI difference beyond minimum ABI and conventional covariates. Weighted MSE gain was -0.000148(m/s)^2; joint stratum-PSU refit bootstrap95% interval[-0.000675,0.000069]. This exploratory negative performance-outcome extension of earlier self-reported limitation work is not clinical equivalence, causal evidence or proof that asymmetry contains no physiology.
